drafted_from: tool:find-faces's own row (its words, input schema, sample runs and steps) and what its sample runs answered here; read it before relying on it
start_here: Say to your AI: "Find every face in a picture or video and name the ones that belong to people who agreed to be known", with {"file":"sample-picture.png"}. It runs tool:find-faces and answers {"faces":[]}
no_lists_because: It names no list of yours: it takes its input and answers, and keeps no row.
instructions: 1. Say to your AI: "Find every face in a picture or video and name the ones that belong to people who agreed to be known", and give it file (The picture or video, by identity in your files).
2. The AI calls run_resource_operation at @workshop-tools with method tools:run, tool tool:find-faces and its input (the worked example shows one).

3. Read what comes back: Finds the faces in a picture, or in a picture taken from a video every few seconds, and answers each face's place (the second, the box in pixels) and who it is: the person's name when one enrolled face is clearly the closest, every person it could be when two are too close to tell, nobody otherwise.
